title: A doorbell the GPU waits on
subtitle: Batches cross from the CPU to the GPU through a pinned ring and a 64-byte doorbell the GPU's stream waits on directly, with no CPU synchronisation; and why that path is used for the extraction engines and left off for the vendor's executor

stats.label: one producer, the filler thread; one consumer, the decode thread
retries of 1 ms on a full ring, then a block; a batch is never dropped
host threads between a publish and the GPU starting work

lede: The batch filler writes a batch into memory the GPU can read directly, and the GPU's stream begins work the instant the batch is published, without a host thread noticing and launching anything. The CUDA driver has a primitive for exactly this, a stream operation that blocks until a 64-bit value in memory reaches a threshold, and the runtime's hot queue is built around it. Batches live in a ring of pinned host memory, mapped for direct GPU access and write-combined for fast CPU writes, with pages pre-faulted at warm-up so no first-touch fault lands on the hot path.
quote: The fastest handoff from a CPU producer to a GPU consumer is one in which neither side waits on the other's clock.
evidence: CUDA driver programming: a stream operation that waits on a 64-byte doorbell in mapped pinned memory, so the GPU starts a batch with no host thread in the loop.
Lock-free and zero-copy data paths: a single-producer single-consumer pinned ring of write-combined, pre-faulted pages that pads at the wrap and never drops a batch, 10 bounded retries then a block.
GPU memory management: the pinned path enabled for a device-reading extraction backend and kept off for a CPU-reading executor, with a counter that fires on a mismatch.
author: Corey James
